rationale: All 564 failures are a single machine account (C2649$@DOM1) authenticating from its own matching host (source C2649) against nine internal servers, with zero successes over ~36 hours. A brute-force actor would cycle accounts or passwords across targets; here the 'cross_source' and 'slow_scan' rules fire only because one host contacts many servers on schedule. No successful login and no lateral indicator warrants analyst action; recommend routine remediation of the host's machine password rather than an incident response.

Single internal source C2621 to single host C586, repeating on a near-exact ~20-minute cadence over 3.7 hours. The pattern (fixed interval, one stale credential, one working credential, no account spraying, no lateral spread) is consistent with a scheduled job or client holding an outdated password rather than an attack.

However, several successes are for accounts this source had never authenticated as before (U453 L202834532, U3064 L202921679) and the failure/success interleaving across multiple hosts leaves credential reuse or lateral movement plausible. Neither dismissal category in policy (generic-name scanning that never succeeds, or a single user mistyping) applies, and the dossier lacks the baseline needed to tell normal multi-user behaviour from an authenticated foothold, so a human should review.
